title: Boab: Ancient Boabs You Can Visit
meta_description: A boab moved 3,200km by truck to Perth, a Kimberley giant wrongly nicknamed a prison, and the tree an 1856 expedition carved its own species name from.
intro: Australia's boab is the only baobab outside Africa and Madagascar, a swollen bottle-trunked tree that drops its leaves for the dry season and photosynthesises through its bark. Its scientific name, Adansonia gregorii, comes from Ferdinand von Mueller naming it after Augustus Gregory, whose 1855 expedition camped beside the Timber Creek tree that still carries the party's carved arrival and departure dates. Derby's so-called Boab Prison Tree carries a legend, colonial prisoners held inside it, that historians have traced to a 1948 newspaper caption rather than any record; what is documented is its real use by the Nyikina and Warrwa people as shelter and burial ground. And Perth's Gija Jumulu, over 750 years old, made the longest recorded road journey of any living tree its size: 3,200km from the Kimberley in 2008, given its name by the Gija people who once stood beside it at home.
